name: English Baseline
expected: Fluent English response explaining wage rights under Payment of Wages Act.
prompt: My employer in Bangalore has not paid my salary for two months.
raw_response:
Hello, I understand how stressful and difficult it is to be without your earned salary for two months.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee working in Bangalore whose employer has withheld your salary for two consecutive months. You are seeking legal remedies under Indian employment laws to recover your unpaid dues.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the succeeding month (or the 10th day if more than 1,000 workers are employed), making the withholding of your two-month salary a direct statutory violation.
- Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 strictly prohibits arbitrary or unauthorized salary deductions and the indefinite withholding of earned wages without a formal, lawful inquiry or order.
- Under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you have the right to approach the designated Authority/Labour Commissioner to claim your delayed wages, along with compensation up to ten times the delayed amount.
- Under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, private and commercial employees in Bangalore are entitled to timely payment of earned salary and complete final settlement upon completion of work periods.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your employment contract, appointment letter, salary slips for previous months, bank statements showing the gap in payments, and any written communication or emails exchanged with your employer regarding the unpaid salary.
2. Send written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal legal demand notice to your employer stating the exact unpaid amount, citing Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, and granting a clear 15-day deadline to clear all dues.
3. Appropriate forum: If the employer fails to pay within the notice period, file an application before the designated Labour Commissioner or Authority under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 in Bangalore.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. What is the total exact amount of unpaid salary for these two months?
2. Do you have an active employment agreement or appointment letter in writing with this employer in Bangalore?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.
